title: Why your battery quietly fades
text: {{1}} time a lithium-ion battery is recharged, millions of ions shuffle {{2}} the two electrodes and back again, and each round trip takes a microscopic toll. Side reactions slowly lock pockets of material {{3}} from the circuit, {{4}} is why a phone that held a day of charge at five years old now surrenders by mid-afternoon. Heat {{5}} long stretches at a full charge speed the decay {{6}}, so packs kept cool and half-charged age far more gracefully. Engineers have responded {{7}} software that holds the cells below a full charge, {{8}} is why your phone sometimes waits at eighty per cent overnight before finishing the job at dawn.
